attempts.label: DANDI:001642
attempts.paper_title: Distinct Neural Representation in the Dorsolateral, Dorsomedial, and Ventral Parts of the Striatum during Fixed- and Free-Choice Tasks
attempts.entry_title: Striatal subregions in fixed- and free-choice tasks (Ito and Doya 2015)
attempts.description: Tests the findings of Ito and Doya (2015) on dandiset 001642, which holds the behaviour and the spike times of units in the dorsolateral, dorsomedial and ventral striatum of seven rats in 86 sessions of a fixed- and free-choice nose-poke task. It covers the trial counts, the extinction tests and decision trees, the comparison of choice models, the counts of phasically active neurons, their event-aligned activity, the mutual information between firing and state, action and reward, the proportions of event-coding neurons, the regression on action values from the FQ-learning model, and the action information by block type.

notebooks.title: Reproducing Ito and Doya (2015) from dandiset 001642

outcomes.statement: The analysis covers 78,107 trials in 86 recording sessions from seven rats, of which 12,185 are single fixed-choice, 22,234 double fixed-choice, 36,292 free-choice and 3505 extinction-test trials.
outcomes.source: Results, opening section, paragraph 2
outcomes.quote: Here, we report the results of all 78,107 trials in 86 recording sessions, performed by seven rats, consisting of 12,185 single fixed-choice trials (16.4%), 22,234 double fixed-choice trials (30.0%), 36,292 free-choice trials (48.9%), and 3505 extinction test trials (4.7%)
outcomes.notes: Reading b (trials with an L/R choice) on the 86 sessions with units gives 75,348 trials from 7 rats, 12,639 single fixed, 22,695 double fixed, 36,496 free-choice and 3518 extinction trials, all within 10% of the paper. Reading a (all 79,431 trials started) puts single fixed (13,485) outside 10%. Over all 87 files reading b misses single fixed (13,417).
deviations: The 87th file, LE115_14, holds behaviour and no units; the 86 recording sessions are taken as the files with units.

outcomes.statement: Completing a block took 22.56 ± 8.70 trials for single fixed-choice blocks, 47.11 ± 20.29 for double fixed-choice blocks and 41.10 ± 27.58 for free-choice blocks (mean ± SD).
outcomes.source: Results, opening section, paragraph 2
outcomes.quote: Numbers of trials required to complete one block were 22.56 ± 8.70 for single fixed-choice blocks, 47.11 ± 20.29 for double fixed-choice blocks, and 41.10 ± 27.58 for free-choice blocks, (mean ± SD)
outcomes.notes: Reading a (choice trials, completed blocks) gives 22.50 ± 8.62 (551 single fixed blocks), 47.15 ± 20.34 (469 double fixed) and 41.05 ± 27.54 (866 free). Readings b and c also match; reading d misses the double fixed SD (22.86).

outcomes.statement: During extinction tests, choice probabilities for the left and right tones differ significantly from those for the choice tone.
outcomes.source: Results, Behavioral performance, paragraph 1; Figure 2B and 2C
outcomes.quote: Choice probabilities during extinction tests were significantly different between the left and right tones and the choice tone (Fig. 2C; p < 0.0001, χ2 test)
outcomes.notes: Over five extinction trials P(left) is 0.822 for the left tone and 0.108 for the right tone, 0.646 and 0.344 for the choice tone after left- and right-optimal blocks. All six chi-square tests (both readings, with and without Yates) give p of 2.4e-16 or less, with the fixed tones further from 0.5. The pooled P(optimal) is higher for the fixed tones in all 7 rats.
deviations: Extinction trials are numbered among the choice trials of each extinction block; wait-error trials are left out.

outcomes.statement: In extinction tests the choice-tone choice probability shifts toward 50% after the first unrewarded trial, while the left- and right-tone choice probabilities stay biased after five unrewarded trials.
outcomes.source: Results, Behavioral performance, paragraph 1; Figure 2B
outcomes.quote: whereas the choice probabilities for the free-choice tone shifted toward 50% following the first nonrewarded trial (orange lines, Fig. 2B), choice probabilities for the left and right tones remained biased even after five no-reward trials
outcomes.notes: Choice-tone P(left) moves from 0.815 to 0.551 (after left-optimal blocks, 119) and from 0.175 to 0.379 (after right-optimal blocks, 103) between trials 1 and 2. At trial 5 the left tone is at 0.818 (Wilson 0.765 to 0.862) and the right tone at 0.155 (0.115 to 0.207); Clopper-Pearson gives the same.

outcomes.statement: Choice-tone choices depend on the previous one or two trials' actions and rewards (a decision tree that expands symmetrically), while left- and right-tone choices stay biased toward left and right whatever the previous experience.
outcomes.source: Results, Behavioral performance, paragraph 2; Figure 2D to 2F
outcomes.quote: The decision tree for choice tones expands symmetrically (Fig. 2D), indicating that action selection was sensitive to past experiences ... action probabilities for the left or right tones (in both single and double fixed-choice blocks) are biased toward 1 (Fig. 2E) or 0 (Fig. 2F), respectively, indicating insensitivity to past experiences
outcomes.notes: Choice tone, P(L) after L1 0.804 (0.796 to 0.812) and after R1 0.185 (0.177 to 0.193). Every left-tone branch at d = 1 and 2 is at 0.699 or more and every right-tone branch at 0.254 or less. All 12 readings hold.
deviations: Whether the choice-tone sequences include the extinction trials is not stated; both are run and agree.

outcomes.statement: Of six DFQ-learning variants and the Markov models, the FQ-learning model with time-varying parameters predicts held-out rat choices in free-choice blocks best.
outcomes.source: Results, Behavioral performance, paragraph 5; Figure 2G
outcomes.quote: found that the FQ-learning model with time-varying parameters predicted rat behaviors best (Fig. 2G). Prediction accuracy was higher than that of Markov models

statistics.about: other models against FQ-learning (variable), as marked in Fig. 2G (which models carry the marks could not be read)

outcomes.notes: Normalized likelihood of test data, alternate and random split: FQ variable 0.5758 and 0.5762, DFQ variable 0.5770 and 0.5775, Markov 3 0.5770 and 0.5782, Markov 4 0.5785 and 0.5797. FQ variable is not the best model and is below Markov 3 and 4 under both splits; per session Markov 4 is above it with Wilcoxon p = 0.026 and 0.0044. Three further particle-filter seeds give FQ variable 0.5757 to 0.5764 and DFQ variable 0.5768 to 0.5775, and a 5 x 5 grid of drift SDs gives FQ variable 0.5760 on the alternate split, all below Markov 4.
deviations: The model equations are missing from the paper's text; the update, choice rule, initial values (0), bounds and the particle-filter priors (alpha uniform on 0 to 1, kappa uniform on 0 to 5, clipped random walks) are assumed as models.py states, and the drift SDs are chosen on a 3 x 3 grid by the training likelihood.
86 sessions with free-choice trials, split 43 and 43, where the paper used 101 training and 101 test sessions.
Markov models use one pseudo-count per action, so unseen sequences give 0.5, and the available shorter history at the start of a session (standard choices).

outcomes.statement: A regular actor-critic model with constant parameters predicts test choices close to chance, with normalized likelihood 0.5080.
outcomes.source: Results, Behavioral performance, last paragraph
outcomes.quote: We also tested a regular actor-critic model with constant variables (Sutton and Barto, 1998), but the normalized likelihood of test data was close to the chance level (0.5080; data not shown)
outcomes.notes: Normalized likelihood of test data 0.5000 (shared rate) and 0.5013 (separate rates) on the alternate split, 0.5026 and 0.5000 on the random split, all within 0.0508 of 0.5080. The fits put the rates or the inverse temperature at or near a bound ([0, 0] and [1, 0, 0] give exactly 0.5), and the tolerance band contains 0.5, so the test cannot tell the model from one that does not learn.
deviations: Constant parameters fitted by maximum likelihood on the training sessions, as in fig2g-fq-variable-best; rates in 0 to 1, inverse temperature in 0 to 50 (standard bounds).

outcomes.statement: Stable recordings were made from 260 DLS, 178 DMS and 179 VS neurons, of which 190, 105 and 119 were phasically active neurons.
outcomes.source: Results, Activity patterns of phasically active neurons, paragraph 1
outcomes.quote: Stable recordings were made from 260 neurons in DLS, 178 neurons in DMS, and 179 neurons in VS from seven rats ... Among these, 190, 105, and 119 neurons from DLS, DMS, and VS, respectively, were classified as PANs
outcomes.notes: The files hold no waveforms, amplitudes or depths (units columns Area, Electrode_ID, Neuron_ID, PANs, Unit_Name, the electrode references and the spike times), so exclusion conditions 1, 2 and 5 cannot be applied. Every count that can be computed misses the paper in at least one region. All units 297, 255, 215 against 260, 178, 179. After condition 3, condition 4 read as all bins below 1 Hz and the duplicate check (90 removed), 233, 204, 142; the PAN rule then gives 183, 147, 119 (DMS outside 10%). Condition 4 read as any bin below 1 Hz leaves 47, 57, 21. The deposited PANs flag gives 204, 112, 138 (VS outside 10%), and the flagged units that pass the computable exclusions 160, 97, 99 (DLS and VS outside). Asked in round 2, the counts without the duplicate check, which are upper limits of the paper's counts under each reading of condition 4 since the missing conditions can only remove units, are under (4i) 265, 224, 169 units and 213, 163, 143 rule PANs, none below the lower end of its tolerance (234, 160.2, 161.1; 171, 94.5, 107.1), and under (4ii) 49, 62, 22 units and 2, 7, 4 PANs, all far below. So no count is shown to miss under reading (4i), and the claim cannot be decided from the dandiset. As tested, the computed counts gave not_reproduced; the change to blocked (data_missing) was proposed after round 2 and agreed in round 3.
deviations: Exclusion conditions 1, 2 and 5 need waveforms or histology and are not applied; the PETH-similarity part of the duplicate rule is not defined and is not applied.

findings.statement: The trial table describes `state` as 1 = Tone A (left), 2 = Tone B (right), 3 = Tone C (choice). The data show 2 = left tone, 3 = right tone and 1 = choice tone: state 2 is the only state in single fixed-choice blocks with rule (50, 0), its right choices are never rewarded (2669 trials), state 3 left choices are never rewarded (2026), and state 1 is the only state in free-choice blocks.

The dandiset holds 859 units (297 DLS, 255 DMS, 215 VS, 92 CS), more than the paper's 617 stable neurons, without a column saying which passed the paper's stability, amplitude, histology and duplicate exclusions. Its `PANs` flag (204, 112, 138 in DLS, DMS, VS) is described as Prop(ISI > 1 s) > 0.4, but 174 units that pass that rule are not flagged, so the flag rests on a further criterion that is not described. 15 CS units are flagged, though the paper analyses only DLS, DMS and VS. 38 flagged units have no PETH above 1 Hz around the three events (exclusion condition 3).
No waveforms, amplitudes or recording depths are deposited, so the paper's exclusion conditions 1, 2 and 5 and its waveform basis for the PAN class cannot be applied.
The dandiset has 87 files for the paper's 86 recording sessions; LE115_14 holds behaviour (802 trials) and no units.
The paper's model comparison used 202 behavioural sessions (101 training, 101 test); the dandiset holds 86 sessions with free-choice trials, so the comparison of Fig. 2G can be run only on these.

Some event times fall outside the task's stated ranges: cue durations (E2 to E3) from 0.009 s where the paper gives 1 to 2 s (1st percentile 1.04 s), centre-poke durations before the cue (E1 to E2) from 0.026 s where the paper gives 500 to 1000 ms (1st percentile 0.51 s), and 942 choice trials lack one of the six events or have them out of order.

Mutual information (Figs. 5, 9, 10): was the plug-in estimate corrected for bias, and if so by the Panzeri and Treves (1996) estimate the Results cite, or by shuffling? How were the four firing levels defined (quartiles of the trial counts?), and were the random events of the threshold drawn with the real proportions? The cue-offset, state, dms-never-above-dls and stay-switch results depend on it.

Fig. 4: which smoothing was applied to the EASHs before normalizing, were extinction trials among the 'whole trials', and does 'reached 0.5 during each trial phase' mean any bin at or above 0.5 in the phase? The DMS against VS test of Phase 5 depends on these.
Fig. 5G: over which bins were the regions' reward information compared (Phase 6, Phases 6 and 7, or the peak)?

Figs. 9 and 10: was action information computed on the last 20 trials of all blocks of a type pooled, or per block and averaged, and is the 'paired-Mann-Whitney U test' the Wilcoxon signed-rank test over neurons? The VS absence of Fig. 10C and the DLS and DMS differences depend on it.

Fig. 8: were the regression windows on the EASH axis or in real time, which seven events were used (E1 to E7 or E0 to E6), were the trials free-choice trials only, and which subsets of regressors were searched (the text gives six variables and 2^6 models for the eight terms listed)? The QR and action-value results of DMS depend on the window axis.
Fig. 6: which window defines state coding (all of Phase 3, or a 500 ms window), and were the windows on the EASH axis or in real time?

Fig. 2G: the update and choice equations, the initial values, and the priors and parameter ranges of the particle filter are images missing from the text or referred to Ito and Doya (2009); how were the 202 sessions split into training and test halves?

disagreements.reason: None of the computable counts limits the paper's counts. The all-unit counts (297, 255, 215) are only upper limits, as exclusions can only lower them. Conditions 1, 2 and 5 cannot be applied and can only remove more units; DMS after the computable exclusions (204, against a limit of 195.8) could still drop into tolerance. The VS count of 142 is not an upper limit either, as the paper removes a pair as duplicates only if the cross-correlogram test passes 'and their PETHs had similar shapes', and the notebook's check omits that part, so its 90 removals may include units the paper kept. If VS after conditions (3) and (4i), with no duplicate removal, fell below 161.1, that would justify not_reproduced under reading 4i; that count is not printed. Under reading 4ii every count is far below the paper (47, 57, 21), so the condition-4 readings disagree too. That blocking would cascade to the dependent claims is a consequence of the outcome, not evidence about it. Would block it as data_missing.

entries.title: Striatal subregions in fixed- and free-choice tasks (Ito and Doya 2015)
entries.description: Tests the findings of Ito and Doya (2015) on dandiset 001642, which holds the behaviour and the spike times of units in the dorsolateral, dorsomedial and ventral striatum of seven rats in 86 sessions of a fixed- and free-choice nose-poke task. It covers the trial counts, the extinction tests and decision trees, the comparison of choice models, the counts of phasically active neurons, their event-aligned activity, the mutual information between firing and state, action and reward, the proportions of event-coding neurons, the regression on action values from the FQ-learning model, and the action information by block type.
